title: Reflection of local finite presentations across surjective closed immersions
statement: Let p:V→U be a surjective closed immersion of schemes, R a monoid object in abelian pro-etale sheaves on U, and M an R-module sheaf. If p* M is locally finitely presented over p* R (a pro-etale covering with finite free cokernel presentations), then M is locally finitely presented over R. This is a reflection statement; no noetherianity, reducedness or uniform nilpotence bound is assumed.

proof.text: Choose a pro-etale cover C of V presenting p* M. Apply exists_cover_refinement_surjective_closed to obtain a pro-etale cover B of U and, for each b, a cartesian square with q:W -> B_b over p and a refinement map r:W -> C_a. Closed immersions and surjective morphisms are stable under base change, so q is again surjective closed.

Apply abelian_closed_support to any surjective closed immersion i and its empty open complement. Every abelian sheaf on that complement is zero, hence the actual inverse-image/direct-image unit and counit are invertible. Lift their components through the forgetful functors using mapModAdjunction_unit_app_hom and mapModAdjunction_counit_app_hom. Thus inverse image on modules over any monoid object R is an additive equivalence, without a commutativity assumption.

Reuse fp_reflect from CondensedSurjectiveClosedLocalPresentation through proof-only import all. It reflects finite free cokernel presentations through additive equivalences identifying regular modules. Reuse the generic finitePresentation_of_iso and finitePresentation_mapMod, and the scalar-isomorphism lemmas finitePresentation_comap and finitePresentation_of_comap, from ProEtaleModuleConstructiblePullback. No duplicate transport lemmas or additional coefficient hypotheses are needed.

Use the proved monoidality instance for upperStarComp.inv from module-constructible-pullback to form mapModCompIso. The ring comparison is an isomorphism, so the imported comap transport identifies finite presentation of a composite pullback with that of an iterated pullback. Pull hC(a) along r and use r followed by C.f(a) = s and the cartesian square equation q followed by B.f(b) = s followed by p. This yields finite presentation after q of M restricted to B_b. Reflect through the module equivalence of step 2. The cover B then witnesses local finite presentation of the original M. Empty covers and rank-zero presentations require no separate nonempty assumption.
